Estimate sea-surface photosynthetically available radiation (PAR)

Source: R/PAR_sea_surface_Wm2.R
PAR_sea_surface_piCurve.Rd

Estimates clear-sky sea-surface photosynthetically available radiation (PAR) over a user-specified wavelength interval using sea_surface_irradiance_piCurve().

PAR_sea_surface_piCurve(
  zenith_angle,
  database_info,
  sample_date,
  H_oz = 266,
  data_climato_solar = NULL,
  lambda_min = 400,
  lambda_max = 700,
  units = c("W m^-2", "umol photons m^-2 s^-1")
)

Source

Gregg, W. W., & Carder, K. L. (1990). A simple spectral solar irradiance model for cloudless maritime atmospheres. Journal of Geophysical Research.

Arguments

zenith_angle

Numeric scalar. Solar zenith angle in degrees (0 <= zenith_angle < 90). Users may estimate solar zenith angle using solar_zenith_angle_piCurve().

database_info

Data frame containing wavelength-specific optical inputs. Must contain the columns required by sea_surface_irradiance_piCurve(). For the built-in dataset, see GreggCarder1990.

sample_date

A date coercible to Date. Used to compute orbital correction of extraterrestrial irradiance.

H_oz

Numeric scalar. Total column ozone depth in Dobson Units (DU). Default is 266.

data_climato_solar

Optional list or one-row data frame of atmospheric inputs. If NULL, default climatological values are used.

lambda_min

Numeric scalar. Lower wavelength bound for PAR integration in nm. Default is 400.

lambda_max

Numeric scalar. Upper wavelength bound for PAR integration in nm. Default is 700.

units

Character string specifying output units. Must be one of "umol photons m^-2 s^-1" or "W m^-2"(default).

Value

A one-row data frame with columns:

lambda_min

Lower wavelength bound of integration (nm).

lambda_max

Upper wavelength bound of integration (nm).

units

Output PAR units.

PAR

Integrated sea-surface PAR in the requested units.

Details

This function first estimates spectral downwelling irradiance at the sea surface using sea_surface_irradiance_piCurve(), then integrates over the photosynthetically active waveband using the trapezoidal rule.

By default, PAR is computed over 400–700 nm.

If units = "W m^-2", spectral irradiance is integrated directly: $$ PAR = \int_{\lambda_{min}}^{\lambda_{max}} E_d(\lambda)\ d\lambda $$

If units = "umol photons m^-2 s^-1", spectral irradiance is first converted to photon flux density at each wavelength: $$ Q(\lambda) = E_d(\lambda)\frac{\lambda \times 10^{-9}}{h c} \times \frac{10^6}{N_A} $$ where \(E_d(\lambda)\) is spectral irradiance, \(h\) is Planck's constant, \(c\) is the speed of light, and \(N_A\) is Avogadro's number. The converted spectrum is then integrated over wavelength.

Because photon energy depends on wavelength, conversion to quantum units must be performed spectrally before integration rather than by applying a single factor to integrated energy-based PAR.

The dataset GreggCarder1990 provides wavelength-specific coefficients consistent with the Gregg and Carder (1990) formulation.

Examples

# Example using Gregg & Carder (1990) dataset
PAR_sea_surface_piCurve(
  zenith_angle = 30,
  database_info = GreggCarder1990,
  sample_date = "2024-07-24"
)
#>   lambda_min lambda_max  units      PAR
#> 1        400        700 W m^-2 388.0663

# Return PAR in energy units
PAR_sea_surface_piCurve(
  zenith_angle = 30,
  database_info = GreggCarder1990,
  sample_date = "2024-07-24",
  units = "umol photons m^-2 s^-1"
)
#>   lambda_min lambda_max                  units      PAR
#> 1        400        700 umol photons m^-2 s^-1 1771.053

# Restrict integration bounds
PAR_sea_surface_piCurve(
  zenith_angle = 30,
  database_info = GreggCarder1990,
  sample_date = "2024-07-24",
  lambda_min = 450,
  lambda_max = 650
)
#>   lambda_min lambda_max  units      PAR
#> 1        450        650 W m^-2 269.3301

# Example based on coordinates and time
DATE <- as.Date("2024-03-20")
zn <- solar_zenith_angle_piCurve(
  DATE,
  time = "12:00:00",
  latitude = 0,
  longitude = 0
)

PAR_sea_surface_piCurve(
  zenith_angle = zn,
  database_info = GreggCarder1990,
  sample_date = DATE
)
#>   lambda_min lambda_max  units     PAR
#> 1        400        700 W m^-2 470.549
